column2: The writing which has always been known by this name is clearly, from internal evidence, a letter sent by the church of Rome to the church of Corinth in consequence of trouble in the latter community which had led to the deposition of certain Presbyters. The church of Rome writes protesting against this deposition, and the partizanship which has caused it.

Johan Bojer was one of Norway’s greatest writers, nominated five times for the Nobel Prize. His 1924 novel, A Pilgrimage, is on the surface the tale of the difficulties faced by Regina, a young unmarried mother in Norway whose son was given to another couple at birth, and her maternal love for her lost child.

Jacob Riis was a Danish photojournalist whose groundbreaking book documented the lives and struggles of working people – many of them recent immigrants – in New York in the late 1880s. His narrative is sensitive but unsparing, and filled with intimate portraits of the men, women, and children of America’s Gilded Age underclass.
